purpose: Suvorexant is used to help adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep. It is a prescription sleep medicine meant to be used short-term. It helps you get to sleep and stay asleep through the night.
how_it_works: Your brain has natural chemicals called orexins that keep you awake and alert. Suvorexant works by blocking those wake-promoting signals in your brain, which helps your body shift into sleep mode. Think of it like gently turning down the 'stay awake' switch in your brain so sleep can happen more naturally.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is feeling drowsy or groggy the next morning. Some people also notice headache, dizziness, or unusual dreams. A small number of people may feel like they cannot move right when they wake up, which usually passes quickly.
warnings: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery the morning after taking this medicine, especially at first, because drowsiness can linger. Avoid alcohol while taking suvorexant, as it can make drowsiness much worse. Rare but serious side effects include sleep-walking, sleep-driving, or doing other activities while asleep without remembering them — stop the medicine and call your doctor right away if this happens. Tell your doctor if you have a history of depression, substance abuse, or breathing problems like sleep apnea.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken within 30 minutes before bedtime, with at least 7 hours remaining before you need to wake up. Your doctor may increase the dose to 20 mg if needed. Never take more than 20 mg in one night, and only take it when you are ready to go to sleep.
